caption: Structure of the project, from the original Moringa oleifera radiobiology investigation to the prioritisation of candidate constituents for future experimental work. Box fills distinguish data sources, computational steps, literature curation and proposed future work; they do not indicate how strong the evidence at each stage is. The Moringa measurements are the biological motivation only: they are never used as training, calibration or validation data, because crystal-violet proliferation under extract treatment and clonogenic survival at 2 Gy are different endpoints. Stage 6 is a proposal, not completed work.

Composition and radiosensitivity of the analysed cohort (241 eligible records, 237 independent biological components). (a) Independent components per tissue (OncotreeLineage); the dashed line marks the ten-component threshold above which a tissue formed its own cross-validation stratum. (b) Distribution of observed CLARIFi mSF2, the literature-median clonogenic surviving fraction at 2 Gy, with one point per independent component so that related cell lines count once; tissues with fewer than ten components are pooled. Boxes show the median and interquartile range; whiskers extend to 1.5 times the interquartile range. Open diamonds mark MCF-7 and DU145, two of the three lines used in the motivating Moringa study, shown as context only: no statement about Moringa extracts or radioprotection is made or implied. V79 is a Chinese hamster line and has no counterpart in this human cohort.

Out-of-fold predictive performance of the five prespecified models (M0 global mean, M1 tissue only, M1P tissue and proliferation, M2 tissue and 50 Hallmark expression scores, M2P tissue, proliferation and expression). (a) Component-weighted mean absolute error, in mSF2 units, with bars starting at zero. (b) Out-of-sample R-squared, where zero corresponds to predicting the training-set mean; every model lies close to zero, so none explains much of the variation between cell lines. (c) Paired difference in MAE in each of the ten cross-validation repeats for the primary comparison (M2 against M1) and the proliferation-adjusted sensitivity comparison (M2P against M1P); positive values favour the richer model. The thick vertical bar is the pooled estimate, the mean over repeats. The upper axis expresses the same difference as a percentage of MAE(M1). Repeats re-split the same 237 components, so their spread shows split-to-split variability, not sampling uncertainty; no interval is shown because no interval method was validated for this design. All values are component-weighted out-of-fold values from ten repeats of five-fold cross-validation grouped by biological component and stratified by tissue, with all tuning and scaling inside training folds. Descriptive only: superiority was not formally assessed and negative-control draws were not run.

Why the out-of-sample R-squared stays near zero. (a, b) Observed against out-of-fold predicted mSF2 for the tissue-only model M1 and the tissue-plus-expression model M2. Each point is one independent biological component; records of a component are averaged and each record's prediction is already the mean over the ten cross-validation repeats, so no cell line contributes more than one point. The dashed line is the identity; both axes span the full possible range of the endpoint. (c) Empirical cumulative distributions of the observed values and of the predictions of both models. The predictions of both models occupy a narrow band near the cohort mean while the observations span almost the whole interval, which is the behaviour of a model with little usable signal rather than of a miscalibrated one. No trend line is fitted. Descriptive only.

Performance by tissue of origin, for the nine tissues with at least ten independent components; the number of components is given beside each tissue name. (a) Component-weighted out-of-fold MAE of each model, in mSF2 units; lighter cells are lower error. (b) The difference MAE(M1) minus MAE(M2) for the same tissues, in the same row order; positive values (blue) mean the expression model had the lower error. Differences are small relative to the errors themselves and are descriptive only: they come from one cross-validated run, no per-tissue inference was performed, and tissues with fewer than ten components are omitted here because their estimates are unstable.

Exploratory importance of the Hallmark gene-set scores in the expression model M2. (a) The fifteen highest-ranked gene sets. Grey points are the grouped permutation importance in each of the fifty model fits (ten repeats by five folds), computed on held-out rows only as the increase in component-weighted MAE when a score is permuted across components; the diamond is the mean over fits, coloured by the prespecified triage tier. The spread across fits is split-to-split variability, not a confidence interval. (b) The two criteria that define tier C, for all fifty gene sets: the share of fits in which importance exceeded zero, and the share of fits in which the set received a non-zero coefficient. The shaded corner is the region satisfying both thresholds (dashed lines, 0.50 each), as frozen in configs/triage.yaml. Tiers A and B were unreachable by design: they require a formally demonstrated prediction gain and at least 1000 negative-control draws, and neither exists in this run. Shares are proportions of overlapping cross-validation fits, not probabilities or p-values. These rankings describe one fitted model family on one dataset. They are not validated biomarkers, causal mechanisms, radiation-response pathways, or molecular effect sizes, and correlated gene-set scores can share or exchange importance.

Cell lines whose measured radiosensitivity the model reproduces least well. (a) Residual (observed minus predicted mSF2 under M2, predictions averaged over repeats) against the observed value, for every measured line, coloured by prespecified discrepancy tier; triangles mark lines carrying at least one technical flag. The strong dependence of the residual on the observed value is shrinkage: because the models predict close to the cohort mean, lines with extreme measured values necessarily have the largest residuals. Circled points are MCF-7 and DU145, labelled because of their relevance to the motivating study; their tiers are not altered. (b) Flags recorded for the tier A and tier B lines, in rank order: flags concerning prediction behaviour (instability across repeats, disagreement between M1 and M2) are distinguished from flags concerning the data or the cell-line identity (stranded RNA profile, related lines in the cohort, a Cellosaurus problem flag on a relative, small tissue group). Tier thresholds are cohort percentiles, so a flag means "relatively large in this cohort", not "abnormal". These are measured CLARIFi lines used in model development, not independent validation samples; a large residual is a signal to re-check identity, data provenance and the original measurement, and is not evidence of unusual radiobiology, radioprotection or radiosensitisation. Lines selected for extreme residuals are expected to agree better on re-measurement even if nothing is wrong (regression to the mean).

Evidence-based prioritisation of documented Moringa oleifera seed and leaf constituents for future experimental work. (a) Points awarded in each of the four prespecified dimensions (numbers are the points; shading is the fraction of that dimension's maximum), beside the extraction-specific evidence: whether the compound has been identified in a dichloromethane extract or fraction of seed or leaf, in seed or leaf with another solvent, or only indirectly. (b) Total priority score out of eight, coloured by tier. The extraction column is deliberately kept outside the score, because the original study used dichloromethane extracts whose composition was never measured. Scoring rules were fixed before any score was computed (docs/compound_protocol.md): only primary studies of the purified compound score, chemical-class analogy earns nothing, several papers from one research group count as one source, a compound with no primary Moringa identification is not assessable, and evidence that a compound protects tumour cells from radiation or is itself genotoxic caps the tier at C. Every tier, including A, is hypothesis-generating: no tier asserts radioprotection, radiosensitisation, potency, or any effect of the extracts used in the original study.

What the published evidence actually links each shortlisted compound to. (a) Radiation-response processes for which a primary study of the purified compound exists: symbol size is the number of independent research groups, and colour distinguishes studies using ionising radiation from studies of the same process without radiation. Compounds are in priority order. An empty row means no qualifying primary study was located, which is a gap in the literature, not evidence of no effect. (b) Where recorded, the number of genes a published experiment measured for the compound that are also members of a Hallmark gene set ranked by the exploratory explainability analysis; blank cells mean no overlap was recorded. Such an overlap marks a point where a compound and a model-highlighted gene set touch the same genes. It is a hypothesis to be tested, not evidence that the compound modifies the gene set, the pathway or clonogenic SF2, and the gene-set ranking it refers to was itself capped at tier C. Reported directions (protection or sensitisation, and the cell type involved) are given in Table C2 and are never merged.

Stability of each cell line's out-of-fold prediction across the ten cross-validation repeats, by model: the distribution over records of the standard deviation of the prediction. Violins show the kernel density over all 241 records with the quartiles marked; the quantity is split-to-split variability of the prediction and is not a prediction interval or a confidence interval, and it widens with the number of repeats. The expression models vary more between splits than the tissue-only models, whose prediction is a shrunken tissue mean.

Spearman correlation between the Hallmark gene-set scores of the tier-C sets and of every set flagged as sharing signal with them (absolute correlation at least 0.80), computed over the eligible cell lines from the expression features alone. Rows and columns follow the triage rank order; no clustering is applied, so no grouping here should be read as a biological relationship. Correlated scores can share or exchange permutation importance, so neighbouring sets in Figure 6 are not independent findings.
